title: There’s a New James Bond, Again. How Did the Last Ones Fare?
summary: The casting of 007 inevitably stokes debate, and the immediate reaction doesn’t necessarily match the eventual reviews.

Now that Robert Pattinson has been[announced as the next James Bond](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/movies/james-bond.html) , fans of the franchise will no doubt weigh in with their verdicts, sizing up the actor and drawing firm conclusions before he even has the chance to make a first impression as 007.


It won’t be the first time. Opining about Bond casting is an age-old pastime, and each actor who has played the world-famous British spy has faced skepticism upon being thrust into this particular spotlight.


And some Bond traditionalists are also wary over what direction the films, based on the novels by Ian Fleming, will take now that the franchise is[controlled by Amazon MGM](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/02/20/business/amazon-james-bond-franchise.html) , which has said that it plans to take the series in new paths.


But hasty complaints and lasting assessments aren’t always the same, and history has been kinder to most Bond stars than the hair-trigger reactions would have suggested.


Here’s a look back at how The New York Times has viewed the previous Bond actors when they were cast and after the films made it to the big screen.
